arguments.draft_body:
## Draft: Q3 SEO content brief, ready for review

This brief covers the onboarding-checklist follow-up post and the pricing page comparison table update discussed this week.

**Onboarding checklist post (draft 2)**
Primary keyword: team onboarding checklist. The post keeps the same structure as the first entry in this series: a short framing paragraph, a numbered checklist, and a downloadable version. Early data shows time on page roughly doubled once the downloadable checklist was added to the first post, so this one repeats that pattern rather than trying something new.

**Pricing page comparison table**
The table now sits directly under the hero, above the product screenshot, matching the layout pattern several competitors have converged on this quarter. The retention-window row still needs a source citation before this can ship; everything else in the table matches the current plan page.

**Social captions**
Recommending we lock in the question-format caption as the standing Tuesday format for at least the next month. Three weeks of data show it beating every other format on Instagram by a wide margin, and the founder-voice LinkedIn posts should stay personal and specific rather than restating the pitch deck.

Open questions are listed below for a quick decision before this goes to design.

## Q3 SEO content brief: onboarding checklist series

Target keyword: "team onboarding checklist". Secondary: "reduce churn in
trial users", "customer onboarding software". Structure: short framing
paragraph, a numbered checklist readers can act on immediately, and a
downloadable version. Competitor pages outrank us here mostly because they
publish longer, more structured guides with tables, so the next post in
this series should keep that shape rather than reverting to narrative
prose.

## Pricing page comparison table, current draft

Row 1: seat limits. Row 2: onboarding support tier. Row 3: API rate limits.
Row 4: data retention window. Row 5: support response time. Placed directly
under the hero, above the existing product screenshot, matching the layout
competitors have converged on this quarter. Legal has flagged the retention
window claim for a source check before this goes live.

## Tuesday caption pattern, three-week trend

Question-format Instagram captions posted on Tuesdays have beaten every
other format for three weeks running, averaging 5.8% engagement against a
3.1% baseline for the rest of the week. The pattern held again this week
with "What's slowing your onboarding down?", forty replies, the highest
count of any caption this quarter.

## Q3 SEO content brief: onboarding checklist series

Target keyword: "team onboarding checklist". Secondary: "reduce churn in
trial users", "customer onboarding software". Structure: short framing
paragraph, a numbered checklist readers can act on immediately, and a
downloadable version. Competitor pages outrank us here mostly because they
publish longer, more structured guides with tables, so the next post in
this series should keep that shape rather than reverting to narrative
prose.

## Pricing page comparison table, current draft

Row 1: seat limits. Row 2: onboarding support tier. Row 3: API rate limits.
Row 4: data retention window. Row 5: support response time. Placed directly
under the hero, above the existing product screenshot, matching the layout
competitors have converged on this quarter. Legal has flagged the retention
window claim for a source check before this goes live.

## Brand voice notes, condensed

Write like a helpful colleague, not a hype machine. Active voice, concrete
nouns, one idea per sentence. Cut "amazing", "revolutionary", and "game
changing" on sight. One exclamation mark per piece, maximum, and only on a
launch day. If it doesn't sound like a person talking to a friend, rewrite
it.

## Tuesday caption pattern, three-week trend

Question-format Instagram captions posted on Tuesdays have beaten every
other format for three weeks running, averaging 5.8% engagement against a
3.1% baseline for the rest of the week. The pattern held again this week
with "What's slowing your onboarding down?", forty replies, the highest
count of any caption this quarter.

## Founder-voice LinkedIn notes

Longer, narrative posts about the founder's background consistently
outperform short feature-announcement posts on LinkedIn. Keep these
personal and specific: a real decision, a real mistake, a real number.
Generic founder content has been the weakest performer two quarters
running, so avoid restating the pitch deck in post form.

## Backlink audit, competitor comparison

Our comparison-content pages are gaining backlinks slower than the
competitor's equivalent pages, mostly because theirs ship with a
downloadable checklist or table that other sites link to directly. Adding
a downloadable asset to our own comparison pages is the highest-leverage
fix identified so far.

## Style guide: numbers and claims

Every specific number or claim in outward-facing copy needs a source we can
point to if asked. Round numbers read as invented; specific ones read as
researched. When in doubt, cite the internal report by name in the review
notes rather than in the copy itself.
